title: Al-Inshiqaq: the sky splits
hookLine: when the sky splits and the earth stretches, O human, you toil toward your Lord (84:1–6)
tomorrow: Al-Inshiqaq: the book in the right hand

lines: A CALLUS, A BURN, A SCAR.
cards: Look at your hands. Maybe there's a callus from a pen, a keyboard, a steering wheel, a guitar string. A burn from a stove.
A scar from a job years ago. Hands keep records of work. Nobody decides to get a callus; it just comes, from doing the same hard thing over and over.

The surah just before Al-Buruj opens with the end of the world, the sky splitting open, the earth stretched flat. Then, out of all that, it turns and speaks to you directly, about exactly that kind of work.

teach.b: Surah eighty-four begins: when the sky splits open. Inshiqaq means a splitting, a cracking apart. The sky, the verse says, listens to its Lord and does what it must.
Then the earth is stretched out, casts out what's inside it, and is left empty. Everything that seemed permanent obeys and opens.

teach.h: O HUMAN — SPOKEN STRAIGHT TO YOU.
teach.b: Then verse six turns to the listener: O human being, you are toiling toward your Lord, with real toil, and you will meet Him. The Arabic word is kadih, from kadh.

teach.h: KADH — TOIL THAT LEAVES A MARK.
teach.b: Not light effort: labor that wears you down and leaves marks, like the callus. Classical dictionaries connect it with scratching or scraping, work that leaves a trace on the one doing it.
So the surah looks at every human life, the commute, the night shift, the diapers, the exam, the grief, and says: all of that is going somewhere.

teach.h: YOU WILL MEET HIM, OR IT.
teach.b: Then: fa-mulaqih, and you will meet Him. Or, some commentators say, you will meet it: your work, face to face. Both readings are held.
Toil here isn't a punishment, and rest isn't wrong. Toil has a direction. You heard it in Al-Layl, efforts differ, and in Al-Ghashiyah, pleased with their effort.

Here it's gathered into one sentence: a life's hard work, pointed toward a meeting. This surah also holds one of the verses where many reciters stop and prostrate, a moment built into the Qur'an itself.

how: Al-Inshiqaq contains one of the Qur'an's places of prostration (84:21), where many reciters and listeners bow to the ground; its line 'O human, you are toiling toward your Lord' is often quoted about the dignity of ordinary work.

o: a gathering of all people on the last day
a splitting open, the sky cracking apart
a turning back, the sinner's repentance

games.q: what's inside the verses — tap the pairs.

s: Al-Inshiqaq calls human toil a punishment
it says the toil is going somewhere: toward your Lord, and a meeting.
verse six speaks directly to the listener: O human
ya ayyuha al-insan, O human: in these exact words, the Qur'an calls out only here and in Al-Infitar (82:6).
this surah contains a place where many reciters prostrate
at 84:21; a hadith reports Abu Hurayra prostrating there.

games.q: the sky has split and the earth stretched flat. the surah turns to you. what does it say you are doing?
games.why: O human, you are toiling toward your Lord, with real toil, and you will meet Him (84:6).

practice: Pick the most tedious task waiting for you, the dishes, the report, the email you've been avoiding, and picture doing it, start to finish. Then see it as part of a long road that's going somewhere, not a pothole in the way.
Settle on doing it with care, as if it counts toward a meeting.

wordCard.voice: Al-Inshiqaq. The splitting, the name of Surah eighty-four: the sky splits, and the human toils toward his Lord. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: "toiling," from k-d-h, hard labor that wears and marks the worker (Qur'an 84:6).

carryVoice: Your line: toiling toward him. Every hard day is on its way somewhere. That's day two hundred six.

sources.ref: Qur'an 84:1–6 (the sky splits and listens; the earth stretched; you are toiling toward your Lord)
Qur'an 84:21 (place of prostration); Sahih al-Bukhari 766 (Abu Hurayra prostrates at this surah)
classical tafsir on 84:6 (meeting your Lord, or your deeds)
